## 2. GAR-GEM-08 · Garage: fluids, capacities, torques and service specs for both vehicles, from their owner's manuals with page numbers

**Due:** 2026-11-26 · **State:** now

**Why:** Garage logs services but cannot tell Joseph what oil, how much, what pressure or what torque. The manuals have it; nothing in Prometheus does.

**What it unlocks:** Every service Garage logs can show the right fluid, capacity and torque for that vehicle, and the tire-pressure check has the placard numbers.

**Read first:**
- https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/garage/
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/pillars/garage/schedule.js (the 2025 Sorento Hybrid owner's manual already used: owners.kia.com document 328-6829)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/pillars/garage/mt07.js (the 2021 Yamaha MT-07)

**Do this:**
1. Manuals: the 2025 Kia Sorento Hybrid US owner's manual (owners.kia.com) and the 2021 Yamaha MT-07 US owner's manual (Yamaha's own manuals site). Give each PDF's URL and its edition/publication code.
2. Sorento Hybrid, 15 rows: engine oil spec and viscosity, oil capacity with filter, coolant type, engine coolant capacity, inverter/HEV coolant if listed, brake fluid spec, automatic transmission fluid spec, fuel tank capacity, minimum octane, tire size, cold tire pressure front, cold tire pressure rear, compact spare pressure, wheel lug nut torque, 12V battery type.
3. MT-07, 15 rows: engine oil spec and viscosity, oil capacity with filter change, oil capacity without, coolant capacity, brake fluid spec, fuel tank capacity, minimum octane, front tire size, rear tire size, front cold pressure, rear cold pressure, drive chain slack range, recommended chain lubricant, spark plug model and gap, rear axle nut torque.
4. page is the manual's printed page number (and the PDF page in brackets). quote is the line that gives the value.

**Make:** `garage_gemini_specs_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array of 30 objects with exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `n` (integer): row
- `vehicle` (text): '2025 Kia Sorento Hybrid' or '2021 Yamaha MT-07'
- `item` (text): as named in steps 2-3
- `value` (text): exactly as the manual gives it
- `unit` (text): qt, L, psi, kPa, lb-ft, N-m, mm, gal, none
- `manual` (text): manual title and edition/publication code
- `page` (text): printed page (PDF page)
- `url` (URL): the PDF
- `quote` (text): the line that gives the value, word for word

## 4. GAR-GEM-10 · Garage: tires for the Grapevine: OE tire, size and load rating for both vehicles, and three winter-capable replacements for the Sorento

**Due:** 2026-11-27 · **State:** now

**Why:** Caltrans chain control R2 lets four-wheel/all-wheel-drive vehicles with snow tires on all four wheels skip chains. Whether the Sorento qualifies depends on its drive and its tires' marking (M+S or the 3PMSF mountain-snowflake symbol). Garage does not know either.

**What it unlocks:** Garage's chain-control card can say whether this car needs chains at R1/R2, and the tire record has the right size and ratings.

**Read first:**
- https://jpavia10.github.io/prometheus-hub/pillars/garage/ (Caltrans chain-control rules)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/main/pillars/garage/schedule.js

**Do this:**
1. From the 2025 Sorento Hybrid owner's manual and Kia's spec page: tire size(s) by trim, the drive (FWD or AWD) per trim, and the OE tire model if Kia names it; from the 2021 MT-07 manual: front and rear tire size and the OE model.
2. Caltrans: quote the R1, R2 and R3 definitions from Caltrans' own chain-control page, including what counts as a snow tire (M+S / 3PMSF).
3. Three replacement tires for the Sorento in its size that carry the 3PMSF symbol (all-weather or winter), from the tire makers' own pages: model, size, load index, speed rating, 3PMSF yes/no, UTQG if any, treadwear warranty (mi).
4. Rows: 1-2 Sorento OE (one per trim size), 3 MT-07 OE, 4-6 Caltrans R1/R2/R3, 7-9 the three replacements.

**Make:** `garage_gemini_tires_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array of 9 objects, exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `n` (integer): row as in step 4
- `kind` (text): oe / caltrans / replacement
- `subject` (text): trim, rule or tire model
- `size` (text): e.g. 235/60R18 103H, or '' for Caltrans rows
- `details` (text): drive, ratings, 3PMSF, warranty or the rule
- `url` (URL): manual PDF, maker page or Caltrans page
- `quote` (text): the line that proves it, word for word

**Before you save, check every one of these yourself:**
- [ ] Every row has a URL you opened yourself today, on the maker's, agency's or store's own site (never a blog, forum, wiki, reseller, or AI summary).
- [ ] Every quote is copied word for word from that page or PDF page and is there now.
- [ ] Every number has its unit in its own field; no number is estimated unless the field says 'math' and shows the arithmetic.
- [ ] No row is a copy of another with the names changed.
- [ ] The file is valid JSON (or exactly the code/markdown asked for) and is named exactly as asked.
